title: Mortals beyond the Horizon
summary: The ordinary people who live in the far Realms.

claims.text: The Union has colonised far Realms for centuries, and some Tradition mages keep families in faerie lands or private Sanctums, so many humans live past the Horizon.
Only exceptional people cope there, trained for life on a Mars colony or in a floating castle; archmages can mix with them freely, since Paradox is little threat.

title: The burdens of archmagehood
summary: Why the greatest mages find little peace.

claims.text: An archmage must mind the gods of the Umbral Courts; a slight to a power such as Tahuti can start a perilous feud.
Nephandi work twice as hard to recruit an archmage, and half the Umbral Courts want help with some crisis.
To an archmage nearly everything becomes an omen, from an early spring to the pattern of broken glass.

title: The Realm of Paradox
summary: A theory of a single Umbral home for Paradox, and the Radiance.

claims.text: Masters of Prime and archmages theorise that the Paradox Realms mages fall into are bubbles in one greater Realm of Paradox, but no one has proved it.
A mage rarely lands in the same Paradox Realm twice, which archmages put down to Paradox shifting to fit each Effect.
The Radiance is a Realm of pure possibility where magic is easier to work and harder to control; even Technomancers find it welcoming if they can get in.
